HRT is the most robust and efficient strategy to reduce waiting time in transit systems.

HBLRT outperforms all other control strategies in terms of passenger waiting time, comfort and reliability to operators, and HBLRT is more effective in reducing excess waiting time than HRT in short headway operations with high passenger demand.
HBLRT is the best strategy to improve transit performance, but it is not always the most convenient one.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
holding and limiting boarding is the most effective control strategy for reducing excess waiting times and increasing reliability.
HBLRT is the best control policy for short headway operation, but in long headway operations HRT is the best choice.
HBLRT provides better performance in terms of comfort, reliability, and operational cost than the other control policies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
holding combined with boarding limitations can be a very effective strategy for improving transit performance.
the use of boarding limit policies can be a powerful tool to reduce the variability of transit operations.
the use of boarding controls in combination with vehicle holding can improve significantly the performance of a transit corridor.
